accepted.title: One of the hardest tensions in early-stage building is speed vs.
accepted.text:
One of the hardest tensions in early-stage building is speed vs. scope.

Every week at Andco, there's a pull to build the ocean. We talk to new law firms and get requests for every workflow a plaintiff firm could ever want - records, bills, liens, claims, seo, marketing, all of it.

That vision is right. It's definitely where we're headed. But it's not what wins.

What wins is shipping absolute killer features. The one thing that makes a managing partner stop mid-demo and say "wait, that's all we have to do?" The feature that saves a case manager 8+ hours on a single file. That's what gets us in the door, gets us referred, and gets us renewed.

So we've been forcing ourselves into a discipline here early on: ship the sharp thing first. Let the platform emerge from a stack of features firms cannot imagine living without.

accepted.title: Lawyers don't call software "beautiful." But ours keep saying it.
accepted.text:
Lawyers don't call software "beautiful." But ours keep saying it. When we ask what they mean, they never mention design, fonts, or colors. 

They describe moments: Requesting records used to mean digging through the police report for the at-fault insurer, rereading intake notes, and combing treatment records for provider names.

In Andco, when users click "Start a request" and most organizations they need to request from are already waiting. When you carry dozens of cases, beauty and convenience are the same word. Beauty is how deeply software understands your day.

We got here by sitting with attorneys and their paralegals, noticing the sigh before every records request, and asking: "What do you do right after this?"

accepted.title: Every Andco customer gets a full client platform included.
accepted.text:
Every Andco customer gets a full client platform included. Here's why we built it.

We kept hearing the same thing from firms: it's hard to get documents from your own client. Weeks of follow-up for something that takes two minutes.

And on the other end of the line, the client is going through the worst stretch of their year. They're hurt, out of work, and anxious. So they call, email, and text to ask where the case stands. Did the medical records come in? The police report? The insurance response? The silence in between is the hardest part.

That part of the workflow needed to be reinvented, not patched.

Most client portals in legal feel like an afterthought. Ours is a full-fledged product. Clean and fast, built for the phone in their pocket, the kind of experience people expect from the apps they use every day, not from a law firm. Clients upload documents and sign forms in a few taps. Or they link their records with us directly through major hospital systems, no paperwork at all. And they can see where their case stands without having to ask.

Everything lands in the case file automatically.

If you're evaluating Andco, you're not just buying agents for records retrieval and insurance verification. You're buying a better experience for people who badly need one. That's the client experience.

accepted.title: The Iran war caused the largest oil supply disruption in history.
accepted.text:
The Iran war caused the largest oil supply disruption in history. Most people assumed the stock market would crash.

It didn't.

When the Strait of Hormuz, the route for roughly a fifth of the world's oil, was blocked, oil ran from around $73 to nearly $120, then fell all the way back to where it started. A full round trip in months. And through all of it, US markets stayed calm and even touched record highs.

So where did the damage actually go?

Not the stock ticker. Prices. US inflation climbed from 2.4% before the war to over 4%. Fuel, shipping, and food all moved with it.

There's a lesson in that for anyone who follows markets: equities tend to look past a shock they believe is temporary. What they fear is duration, how long higher costs linger and feed inflation. The war made the headlines. The inflation is what quietly stayed.

We broke the whole story down in detail, link in the comments.

For educational purposes only. Not investment advice. Figures approximate.
#iranwar #globalmarkets #marketcrash

accepted.title: Indonesians make up ~30% of the entire global factory workforce for Nike and Adidas.
accepted.text:
Indonesians make up ~30% of the entire global factory workforce for Nike and Adidas.

Many founders ask me whether Indonesia has the manufacturing capability for their category. Whether the workforce is skilled enough and if the infrastructure can handle real volume.

Nike and Adidas already answered that question. At scale. For decades.
When a third of the people making shoes for two companies with a combined market cap in the hundreds of billions are in Indonesia, the capability question is closed. 

What is left is an access question. 

Most small and mid-sized American brands have never had a way into that ecosystem. 

The factories that supply Nike are not the factories that show up on a basic Alibaba search, and they were never built to take cold inbound from a brand doing a few thousand units.

This is the gap between what Indonesia is and how it gets discovered. 
The capacity and skilled workforce is there and at a scale most countries cannot match. What has been missing is the layer that connects that capacity to the brands that need it but do not have the relationships, the language, or the years on the ground to access it directly.

Saudara is an AI-native sourcing broker connecting US brands with vetted overseas manufacturers, starting with Indonesia. 

If your category is one where Indonesia already has deep manufacturing experience, even if you have never thought of it as an option, reach out.

#Saudara #Sourcing #Startup

accepted.title: A founder on Reddit gave the most honest sourcing advice I've seen in a while.
accepted.text:
A founder on Reddit gave the most honest sourcing advice I've seen in a while. 
He is right. This is the single most reliable way to know what you are actually working with. 

In person, you see whether there is real machinery or just a desk and a sample room. You see the workers, the floor, the inventory. 

But notice what the advice actually requires. A flight to China. Time off from running the business. Enough familiarity with the language, the industrial zones, and the etiquette to walk into a factory and ask the right questions. 

For a founder running a $2M brand with a small team, that is not a quick trip. It is a significant bet of time and money on top of the sourcing decision itself.
This is the part of the sourcing process that never makes it into the "how to find a factory" guides. The advice that actually works is also the advice that is hardest to act on.

What we do at Saudara is built around that gap.
 We are already on the ground in Indonesia. The factory visits, the in-person vetting, the conversations that reveal whether you are talking to a real manufacturer or a trading company with a nice photo gallery, that work is already done before you ever talk to us. 

You get the outcome of flying there yourself without needing to be the one on the plane.

Saudara is an AI-native sourcing broker connecting US brands with vetted overseas manufacturers, starting with Indonesia. If you have been putting off a sourcing trip because you simply do not have the time, that is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

#saudara #sourcing #startup

For a founder running a $2M brand with a small team, that is not a quick trip. It is a significant bet of time and money on top of the sourcing decision itself.
This is the part of the sourcing process that never makes it into the "how to find a factory" guides. The advice that actually works is also the advice that is hardest to act on.

What we do at Saudara is built around that gap.
 We are already on the ground in Indonesia. The factory visits, the in-person vetting, the conversations that reveal whether you are talking to a real manufacturer or a trading company with a nice photo gallery, that work is already done before you ever talk to us. 

You get the outcome of flying there yourself without needing to be the one on the plane.

Saudara is an AI-native sourcing broker connecting US brands with vetted overseas manufacturers, starting with Indonesia. If you have been putting off a sourcing trip because you simply do not have the time, that is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

Crazy, we went from wanting to bootstrap less than 3 months ago to being in the most successful accelerator in the world.

The timing with AI and the problem we are solving were too strong to ignore, so we decided to go all in.

That is why we are building Pavoot (YC P26) 🦚. We are using AI to automate event management and help companies make sure their events actually drive revenue and improve customer experience.

Super grateful to David Lieb and Grey Baker for betting on us!

We will share more soon about how we met, what YC is like, and what we are building next. Follow to be part of the journey. 🎊

accepted.title: I came across the profile of Ethnicraft, one of the most respected furniture brands manufacturing out of Indonesia, and I loved the founder’s story.
accepted.text:
I came across the profile of Ethnicraft, one of the most respected furniture brands manufacturing out of Indonesia, and I loved the founder’s story.

Philippe Delaisse was enchanted by teak objects he came across while traveling in Bali in 1995, and began exporting antiques and local crafts before quickly moving into production. 

He started in 1996 in Rembang, East Java, where he found skilled woodworkers willing to work with recycled teak taken from old buildings, craftsmen using basic tools, many of them working barefoot. 

From there, piece by piece, he and his business partner built what Ethnicraft is today. 

That operation now runs a main hub of around 1,600 workers in the coastal town of Tegal, combining high-precision machinery and modern production lines with a dedication to material and craft that remains rooted in tradition.
Indonesia has a large young labor force, abundant natural resources, and deep pockets of craft expertise: woodworking being one of them, in a country where a former president built his fortune selling furniture to the world. 

Ethnicraft proves the opportunity is real. It also proves the access problem is real. 

What took Delaisse three decades of being there, in person, building relationships one workshop at a time, is what we built Saudara to compress.
Saudara is an AI-native sourcing broker connecting US brands with vetted overseas manufacturers, starting with Indonesia. 

If you are looking at Indonesian manufacturing for your category and want a head start on that thirty-year head start, reach out.

#Saudara #Sourcing #Startup

It learns your context, your metrics, your definitions so you can just ask questions and get real answers. It will even track your metrics for you and investigate when they fall.

If your team is still waiting on analysts or drowning in dashboards, come talk to me. DMs are open.
